 Oral Order

In this writ petition, petitioners have sought for writ of mandamus to declare that the Scheme Of Acquisition of Lands of the petitioners as lapsed under Section 27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 (hereinafter referred to as BDA Act) and to quash the Preliminary Notification dated 26.01.1989 (Annexure-E) and Final Notification dated 19.01.1994 (Annexure-F) issued by the respondent-authorities.

2. Relevant facts for adjudication of the case as averred in the writ petition are that, the father of the petitioners-S.Narayana Reddy had purchased an extent of 26 guntas of land in Sy No.45/7; 27 guntas of land in Sy No.44/9, totally measuring 01 acre, 13 guntas situate at Valagerahalli Village,
Bangalore South Taluk as per registered Sale Deed produced at Annexure-A. Father of the petitioners died on 15.08.2007 and thereafter, the petitioners are in NC: 2024:KHC:45895 possession of the land in question.

It is pleaded in the writ petition that, the respondent-authorities have issued Preliminary Notification dated 26.01.1989 under Section 17 (1) of the BDA Act, for the purpose of formation of residential layout called as 'Jnanabharati Layout', as per Annexure-E.
Thereafter, the respondent-authorities have passed Final Notification as per Section 19 (1) of the BDA Act as per Annexure-F.
In the above notifications the land in question belonging to the petitioners has been notified for acquisition.

It is the case of the petitioners that, the respondent-Bangalore Development Authority (for short, BDA) has not implemented the Scheme of Acquisition and as such, father of the petitioners during his life time formed layout and sold some of the houses in the subject land by obtaining plan from the Municipal Authorities.
It is the grievance of the petitioners that, the respondent-BDA has not taken NC: 2024:KHC:45895 possession of the land in question and have abandoned the scheme.

Therefore, it is contended in the writ petition that, as per Section 27 of the BDA Act, the acquisition proceedings become lapsed and inoperative and as such, the petitioners have sought for that the impugned notifications are to be quashed on account of not implementing the proposed Acquisition Scheme within reasonable period.
Hence, the petitioners have filed this writ petition.
3. I have heard Sri. K.B.Monesh Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners; Sri.
Ravindranath B., learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the respondent-State and Sri. Murugesh V.Charati, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA.

4. Sri. K.B.Monesh Kumar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners refers to the Notifications at Annexures-E and F and contended that, the NC: 2024:KHC:45895 respondent-authorities have not implemented the scheme and taken possession of the subject land and therefore, the entire scheme has became lapsed under Section 27 of the BDA Act.

It is also contended by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that, no document has been produced by the respondent-BDA with regard to the scheme of development of Layout and further, he refers to the Judgment of this Court in W.P. No.10962 of 2012 and connected writ petitions disposed of on 18.12.2012 (Annexure-H) and argued that, this Court having taken note of the entire aspects of the matter,
under identical circumstances, has allowed the writ petitions and the said order of the learned Single Judge was confirmed by the Division Bench in W.A.No.187-88 of 2017 and connected matters disposed of on 10.04.2019 as per Annexure-J and accordingly, submitted that, there is no justification for the respondent-BDA to hold that the NC: 2024:KHC:45895 scheme has been implemented.

Further, learned counsel appearing for the petitioners also refers to the order dated 04.02.2020 passed by this Court in W.A.No.6838 of 2017 (Annexure-K), particularly, referring to paragraph 8 of the said order, he submitted that, the respondent-authorities are required to implement the scheme within a period of five years from the date of publication in the Official Gazette of the declaration under Section 19(1) of the BDA Act and therefore, he submitted that the prayer made in the writ petition is to be accepted.

It is also the submission of the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that the petitioners herein have sold some of the sites formed in Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/
3 Sy.No.45/7 and Sy.No.44/9 of Valagerahalli Village and entire land in question is a built up area,
houses have been constructed long time back and some of the purchasers of the plots are in possession of the NC: 2024:KHC:45895 schedule land and therefore, the impugned notifications be held as invalid insofar as the subject land is concerned.

Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners also invited the attention of the Court to the photographs produced at Annexure-G and the affidavit filed by the petitioner No.3 on 04.11.2024 during the course of the proceedings and submitted that, a full fledge Layout has been formed including the roads and culverts and accordingly, sought for allowing the writ petition.
5.

Per contra, Sri. Murugesh V. Charati, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA submitted that, as the petitioners herein have formed a Layout and sold sites to the individuals and therefore, even though the petitioners stated that they were in possession of the land in question

,
the said submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners cannot be accepted.
It is also NC: 2024:KHC:45895 submitted that the subsequent purchasers have no right to claim lapse of acquisition proceedings.

It is also the specific contention of the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA that, the respondent-BDA has allotted sites in respect of the land bearing Sy.Nos.44 and 45 of Valagerahalli Village, Kengeri Hobli, Bengaluru South Taluk and therefore, no interference is called for in this writ petition.

It is also argued by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA by referring to statement of objections that, the Land Acquisition Officer has passed Award as per Annexure-R19 and Mahazar has been drawn for taking possession as per Annexure-R20 and the compensation amount has been deposited before the Civil Court as per Annexure-R22 and in that view of the matter, no interference is called for in this writ petition.
Accordingly, sought for dismissal of the writ petition.

In the light of the submissions made by the learned counsel appearing for the parties, it is not in dispute that the father of the petitioners had purchased the land in question as per the registered Sale Deed produced at Annexure-A, dated 29.05.1989.
The Notifications at Annexures-E and F came to be issued on 26.01.1989 and 19.01.1994 respectively and as per the contention of the respondent-BDA, Award has been passed on 07.09.1994.

Perusal of the writ petition would indicate that father of the petitioners is a subsequent purchaser of the land in question, however, the Division Bench of this Court in W.A. No.6838 of 2017, at paragraph 9, held that the subsequent purchaser has right to claim declaration as to scheme having become lapsed.
However, the subsequent purchaser cannot challenge the acquisition proceedings.

- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 Paragraph 9 in W.A.6838 of 2017 (Annexure-K) reads as under:
"9.
In the instant case, there has been an inordinate delay of much more than 5 years.

As per Section 27 of the BDA Act, the said 5 years had long expired before respondent Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/
4 no.1 herein filed the writ petitions in the year 2014.

sentences.text: Of 137 acres 8 1/2 guntas, the award has been passed only in respect of 25 acres 5 guntas and possession appears to have been taken only in respect of 16 acres.
The scheme has definitely not been substantially implemented.
The lands of respondent no.1 herein have not been taken possession of by the BDA.

Further, as rightly observed by the learned Single Judge,
even if respondent no.1 herein is the subsequent purchaser after the notifications were issued, her right to seek declaration as to the scheme having lapsed is not taken away.
It may be that she may not be in a position to challenge the acquisition, but she is certainly entitled for a declaration that the scheme has lapsed."

10. It is also to be noted that, Hon'ble Supreme Court in SLA No.19776 of 2019, by order dated 12.10.2022, arising out of the order dated 16.08.2018 - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 in W.A. No.6936 of 2017 passed by the Division Bench of this Court, wherein the Division Bench has confirmed the order dated 18.09.2017 in W.P. No.55991 of 2015.

Paragraph 7 in the order dated 18.09.2017 in W.P.No.55991 of 2015, reads as under:
"7.

What emerges from the above is, that out of total extent of land acquired as per the final notification measuring 388.09 acres situated at Hulimavu village, an extent of 117.01 acres of land was allegedly handed over to engineering division of the BDA and only in 31.02 acres of land layout was formed and the remaining area of 85.99 acres was covered with built up area.

Similarly, out of 174.25 acres of land situated in Arakere village, 45.04 acres was handed over to engineering section and only in 7.20 acres layout was formed because the remaining extent if 37.84 was built up area.

Thus, out of total extent of 562.34 acres of land acquired as per the final notification,
only 38.22 acres, layout was formed.
Indeed, this is evident from Annexure-R5 produced by the BDA itself along with the statement of objections.
Hence, there was no substantial compliance and completion of the scheme for BTM 6th Stage layout.

It is for this reason, this Court has already held in W.P.Nos. 17421-432/2012 c/w - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 W.P.Nos.2513/2013 2942-46/2013 and W.P.No.18362/2013 disposed on 16.12.2013 that there was no substantial implementation of the scheme.
This Court has, therefore, held in the aforesaid decision that the scheme in respect of the lands which were subject matter of the said writ petitions had lapsed.
Indeed, in W.P.No.18362/2013 referred to herein above the subject matter of the land was Sy.
No.47/1 measuring 3 acres 7 guntas, whereas in the present writ petition land involved is Sy. No.47/2 which is part of old Sy. No. 47.

Though it is contended by the BDA that possession of this land was taken over on 01.12.1990 as per the mahazar produced at Annexure-R3, a perusal of Annexure-K3 does not disclose signature of either the owner of the land or any of the witnesses as held by this Court in Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/
5 W.P.No.2905/2016 that such possession of land was not taken over on 11.12.1990.

sentences.text: Mahazars drawn by the BDA did not evidence taking over possession of the land as asserted by the BDA is evident from the following circumstances.

(a) that Annexure-I) - communication addressed by the Deputy Commissioner for Land Acquisition, BDA, to the State Government, Department of Urban Development discloses that Sy. No.47/2 along with Sy. Nos.45, 46/1, 48/2, 50/2, 50/3 and - 14 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 51/1 were taken possession of by clearing the constructions on 09.01.2010 and a layout had been formed.

(b) Quite contrary to this communication, as per Annexures-E & El notifications issued under Section 48 of the Land Acquisition Act on 05.06.2010 and 13.09.2010, respectively, it is have been deleted from the acquisition.

Had it been that possession of these lands were indeed taken on 09.01.2010 by allegedly clearing the.. constructions put up thereon, BDA and the State Government could not have deleted the adjoining lands from the acquisition.

c) Annexure-R4 - layout plan produced by the BDA along with the statement of objections was apparently not acted upon because though this plan is termed as modified layout plan for BTM 6th Stage, it pertains to 130 acres of land in Hulimavu, whereas admittedly only in 31 acres of Hulimavu village layout has been formed as is apparent from Annexure-R5.

There is no other modified plan or map produced by the BDA to show that in the layout formed utilizing 31 acres of land of Hulimavu,
the land in question bearing Sy. No.47/2 is included.
It is not the case of the BDA that - 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 sites formed in this layout utilizing 31 acres formed part of Sy. No.47/1.
It cannot be so is also demonstrated by the petitioner by producing Annexure-K village map which discloses that entire surrounding area has been either de-notified or excluded from acquisition.
As can be seen from Annexure-K, Sy. No.47 is and 44 and as also Sy. No.49.

Petitioner has Annexures-E & E1 demonstrated by producing copies of the de-notifications that Sy. Nos.46/1, 45,
50/3 & 52 have been de-notified.
Petitioner has averred that in Sy.No.49, the State Government has sold a portion of the land by conducting public auction.

The averrnents made by the petitioner with regard to Annexure-K village map produced by him specifically urging that all the surrounding lands of the land in question Sy. No.47/2 have been excluded from acquisition has not been denied.
d) It is relevant to point out here that in respect of Sy. No.47/2 and the lands de- notified as per Annexures-E & E1, 16(2) notification was issued on 30.01.1992.

If that is so and if indeed,
possession of the land in question along with other surrounding lands had been taken prior to Section 16(2)
- 16 - Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/
6 NC: 2024:KHC:45895 notification, there was absolutely no room for the BDA and the State Government to exclude the surrounding lands by de-notifying them.

sentences.text: Therefore, it is clear that the assertion made by the BDA that possession of this land was taken over in the year 1990 is not correct.

e) Petitioner has rightly contended that when all the surrounding lands have been de- notified or excluded and when layout has not been formed by taking over possession of the land and particularly when only 31 acres has been utilized for formation of layout out of 388 acres of land acquired for BTM 6th Stage in Hulimavu village, the scheme has to be declared as lapsed.

Indeed,
such a declaration has been made in respect of the adjoining lands which are part of the same final notification acquired for implementing the same scheme.

Therefore, despite the fact that petitioner had at one point of time received the compensation, but re-deposited the same along with interest,
as the land has not been utilized by the BDA for formation of layout and as all the surrounded lands have either been de- notified or excluded, petitioner is entitled to succeed in the writ petition."

It is also to be noted that the father of the petitioners has formed Layout by securing permission from the Municipal Authority and Plan Sanction has been made in this regard and residential houses are formed in the schedule property as per the photographs produced at Annexure-G series.

It is also to be noted that, even if the Award came to be passed on 07.09.1994, as per the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA, compensation amount has been deposited before the Principal City Civil Court, Bangalore on 31.07.2000 (Annexure-R21 and R22)
and this would makes it clear that, no deposit of compensation has been made for more than eleven years after passing of Preliminary Notification and six years from the date of passing of the Award.

It is also to be noted from Annexure-N series that, BBMP has issued khata certificate in favour of the respective site owners and - 18 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 therefore, it has to be concluded that the possession of the land in question has not been taken by the respondent-authorities.

I have also noticed from the affidavit dated 04.11.2024 filed by the petitioner No.3, wherein, it is stated that, though bits of land have been sold by the petitioners herein after forming sites, and several residential buildings have been constructed as it is evident from the photographs annexed to the affidavit.

Though the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA filed memo relating to allotment of sites in the schedule land, however, the details enclosed in the said memo dated 04.11.2024 makes it clear that the respondent-BDA has not substantially allotted sites in favour of the needy allottees and further, no allotment has been made for more than 80% of the land in question.

In that view of the matter, though the learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA would submits that,
- 19 - Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/
7 NC: 2024:KHC:45895 the petitioners being subsequent purchasers have no right to question the acquisition proceedings, however, in a peculiar circumstance of this nature, wherein, the Layout has been formed and several site owners have constructed house and that apart, the respondent-BDA has not taken possession of the schedule land and have shown that the Award amount has been deposited after six years from the passing of Award dated 07.09.1994 would substantiate the fact that the respondent-BDA has not made any effort to implement the scheme as stated in the Notifications produced at Annexure-E and F, in terms of Section 27 and 36 of the Act.

sentences.text: At this juncture, it is to be noted that respondent-Acquiring Authority is required to deposit payment of compensation in favour of the persons interested and entitled to, immediately.

In this regard, it is relevant to cite the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Delhi - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 Development Authority vs. Sukhbir Singh and others reported in (2016) 16 SCC 258 and paragraph 9 of the judgment reads as under:
"9.

entities.text: Delhi - 20 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 Development Authority vs. Sukhbir Singh and others reported in (2016) 16 SCC 258
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The scheme of the Land Acquisition Act, insofar as the making of award and the payment of compensation to persons interested, is as follows.
On the day fixed, the Collector after the inquiry that is contemplated under Section 11, has to make an award which must contain the necessary ingredients mentioned in Section 11.
As soon as the award is made, under Section 12(2) of the Act, the Collector is to give immediate notice of the award to such of the persons interested as are not present personally.

This provision, when read with Section 31 of the Act, makes it clear that the statutory scheme is that the Collector is to tender payment of compensation awarded by him to the persons who are interested and entitled thereto, according to the award, on the date of making the award itself.
It is, therefore, clear that under the statutory scheme, the Collector must be armed with the amount of compensation payable to persons interested as soon as the award is made.
Such persons have to be paid the sum mentioned in the award, it being well settled that the award is only an offer which may be accepted or rejected by the claimants.
If accepted, whether under protest or otherwise, it is the duty of the Collector to make payment as soon as - 21 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 possible after making the award.

It is only in a situation where the persons interested refuse consent to receive monies payable, or there be no person competent to alienate the land, or if there be any dispute as to title to receive compensation or its apportionment, is the Collector to deposit the amount of compensation in the Reference Court.
It is only after these steps have been taken that the Collector may take possession of the land, which shall thereupon vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances.

The Act further makes it clear, on a reading of Section 34, that where such compensation is neither paid or deposited on or before taking possession of the land, interest is payable @ 9% p.a. for one year and 15% p.a. thereafter.

This is because a person becomes divested of both possession and Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/
8 title to his property without compensation having been paid or deposited, as the case may be.

sentences.text: This statutory scheme has been adverted to in some of the decisions of this Court.

9.1. In New Reviera Coop. Housing Society v. Land Acquisition Officer [New Reviera Coop. Housing Society v. Land Acquisition Officer, (1996) 1 SCC 731] , SCC at para 3,
this Court held : (SCC p. 733) "3. ...

Once the award has been made and compensation has been deposited or paid under Section 31 of the Act, the Land Acquisition Officer is entitled to take possession and the possession thereby taken stands vested in the State under - 22 -  NC: 2024:KHC:45895 Section 16 of the Act free from all  encumbrances."
9.2.
In Sunder v. Union of India [Sunder v. Union of India, (2001) 7 SCC 211] , SCC at para 24, this Court held : (SCC p. 230) "24. ...

sentences.text: What the legislature intended was to make the aggregate amount under Section 23 of the Act to reach the hands of the person as and when the award is passed, at any rate as soon as he is deprived of the possession of his land.
Any delay in making payment of the said sum should enable the party to have interest on the said sum until he receives the payment.

Splitting up the compensation into different components for the purpose of payment of interest under Section 34 was not in the contemplation of the legislature when that section was framed or enacted."
9.3.

In Bangalore Development Authority v. R. Hanumaiah [Bangalore Development Authority v. R.
Hanumaiah, (2005) 12 SCC 508]

Section 31 contemplates that on making of an award under Section 11 the Collector shall tender amount of compensation awarded by him to the person interested and entitled thereto according to the award and - 23 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 shall pay to them unless prevented by any one or more of the contingencies mentioned in the subsequent clauses.
None of those contingencies arose in the present case.

Thus,
once the amount was tendered and paid the acquisition process was complete.

After making the award under Section 11 the Collector can take possession of the land under Section 16 which shall Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/

The acquisition process stood completed."

12. Following the declaration of law made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, I am of the view that, in the present case no compensation was deposited before the competent court immediately after issuance of the impugned notifications and deposit of compensation amount was made only after eleven years from the date of notifications and therefore, I find force in the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that the respondent-BDA has not taken immediate steps to complete the entire proceedings.

Recently, this Court under similar circumstances in W.P.No.10824 of 2009 disposed of on 06.10.2020, after considering the entire material on record, quashed the impugned Notification therein, holding that the respondent-BDA has not implemented the scheme as required under Section 27 of the BDA Act.

In that view of the matter, as the land in question has been fully developed and petitioners along with other occupants had constructed the house and residing in the said house for more than two decades, taking into consideration the peculiar circumstances of the case on hand, I am of the view that, the writ petition deserves to be allowed.

It is also to be noted that the finding recorded in this writ petition cannot be considered as precedent for any other subsequent cases as this is peculiar circumstance of the case which is evident from the photographs that the land has been fully developed - 25 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 and people are residing in the houses for more than two decades, and as such, at this juncture, it is not expedient to dismiss the petition on the ground that the scheme has been implemented substantially.
In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER (
i) Writ petition is allowed.

(ii) Writ of mandamus is issued to declare that the scheme of acquisition of the land of the petitioners is deemed to have lapsed and inoperative in view of non implementation of the scheme as per Section 27 of the BDA Act and accordingly,
Preliminary Notification dated 26.01.1989 (Annexure-E) and Final Notification dated 19.01.1994 (Annexure- F) issued by the respondent - authorities Smt. Jayalakshmi Reddy vs Bengaluru Development Authority on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176207733/
10 - 26 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 are quashed in respect of the subject land in this writ petition.

opennyai_summary.facts:
In this writ petition, petitioners have sought for writ of mandamus to declare that the Scheme Of Acquisition of Lands of the petitioners as lapsed under Section 27 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976 (hereinafter referred to as BDA Act) and to quash the Preliminary Notification dated 26.01.1989 (Annexure-E) and Final Notification dated 19.01.1994 (Annexure-F) issued by the respondent-authorities.
It is pleaded in the writ petition that, the respondent-authorities have issued Preliminary Notification dated 26.01.1989 under Section 17 (1) of the BDA Act, for the purpose of formation of residential layout called as 'Jnanabharati Layout', as per Annexure-E.
Thereafter, the respondent-authorities have passed Final Notification as per Section 19 (1) of the BDA Act as per Annexure-F.
In the above notifications the land in question belonging to the petitioners has been notified for acquisition.
It is the case of the petitioners that, the respondent-Bangalore Development Authority (for short, BDA) has not implemented the Scheme of Acquisition and as such, father of the petitioners during his life time formed layout and sold some of the houses in the subject land by obtaining plan from the Municipal Authorities.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Therefore, it is contended in the writ petition that, as per Section 27 of the BDA Act, the acquisition proceedings become lapsed and inoperative and as such, the petitioners have sought for that the impugned notifications are to be quashed on account of not implementing the proposed Acquisition Scheme within reasonable period.
Per contra, Sri. Murugesh V. Charati, learned counsel appearing for the respondent-BDA submitted that, as the petitioners herein have formed a Layout and sold sites to the individuals and therefore, even though the petitioners stated that they were in possession of the land in question
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Perusal of the writ petition would indicate that father of the petitioners is a subsequent purchaser of the land in question, however, the Division Bench of this Court in W.A. No.6838 of 2017, at paragraph 9, held that the subsequent purchaser has right to claim declaration as to scheme having become lapsed.
However, the subsequent purchaser cannot challenge the acquisition proceedings.
Hence, there was no substantial compliance and completion of the scheme for BTM 6th Stage layout.
Mahazars drawn by the BDA did not evidence taking over possession of the land as asserted by the BDA is evident from the following circumstances.
It is, therefore, clear that under the statutory scheme, the Collector must be armed with the amount of compensation payable to persons interested as soon as the award is made.
Such persons have to be paid the sum mentioned in the award, it being well settled that the award is only an offer which may be accepted or rejected by the claimants.
If accepted, whether under protest or otherwise, it is the duty of the Collector to make payment as soon as - 21 - NC: 2024:KHC:45895 possible after making the award.
It is only in a situation where the persons interested refuse consent to receive monies payable, or there be no person competent to alienate the land, or if there be any dispute as to title to receive compensation or its apportionment, is the Collector to deposit the amount of compensation in the Reference Court.
9.1. In New Reviera Coop. Housing Society v. Land Acquisition Officer [New Reviera Coop. Housing Society v. Land Acquisition Officer, (1996) 1 SCC 731] , SCC at para 3,
this Court held : (SCC p. 733) "3. ...
In Bangalore Development Authority v. R. Hanumaiah [Bangalore Development Authority v. R.
Hanumaiah, (2005) 12 SCC 508]
The acquisition process stood completed."
12. Following the declaration of law made by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, I am of the view that, in the present case no compensation was deposited before the competent court immediately after issuance of the impugned notifications and deposit of compensation amount was made only after eleven years from the date of notifications and therefore, I find force in the submission made by the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners that the respondent-BDA has not taken immediate steps to complete the entire proceedings.
Recently, this Court under similar circumstances in W.P.No.10824 of 2009 disposed of on 06.10.2020, after considering the entire material on record, quashed the impugned Notification therein, holding that the respondent-BDA has not implemented the scheme as required under Section 27 of the BDA Act.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In the result, I pass the following:
ORDER (
i) Writ petition is allowed.
(ii) Writ of mandamus is issued to declare that the scheme of acquisition of the land of the petitioners is deemed to have lapsed and inoperative in view of non implementation of the scheme as per Section 27 of the BDA Act and accordingly,
